job.title: IT Operations and Cloud Services Manager
job.description:
About the Business 
HWLE is one of Australia's fastest-growing law firms. It has grown by nearly 20% in just over a year, with revenue growing alongside side headcount with more than 2,000 people across nine offices. Growth on that scale needs technology that can keep pace, and the firm is investing to make sure it does. That makes this a rare moment to join. The platform is being built for the next stage of the firm, and the person in this role will help build it.
  
Who you will work for
Most people choose a role for the company. The best career moves are made for the leader. You will report directly to Sam Sofianos, CIO, a heavyweight of legal technology with more than 20 years in professional services. Sam has a strong track record of developing people, with a number of his former team members now in leadership roles and is known as a great leader to work for.
  
About the Role
This is a role with genuine scope. You will lead a national team and own the firm's IT operations, cloud services and core infrastructure, from Windows server, VMware and two onpremises data centres through to LAN/WAN, Fortinet, Azure migrations, backup and disaster recovery. With a direct line to the CIO, your work will be visible at the top of the technology function from day one, and your first 100 days are yours to shape: assess the environment, set the roadmap and deliver the improvements that define the next stage.
  
About You
You are an IT operations or infrastructure leader from a complex, multi-site environment, with strong Windows, networking and Azure expertise and a real passion for developing people. You might be ready for your first role reporting directly to a CIO, or simply looking for the right leader to learn from. Professional services or partnership experience is highly regarded.
  
Why This Role
  •  Report directly to a CIO with a genuine track record of growing future leaders
  • Join a firm in growth that is investing in its technology function
  • Real scope to shape a critical national IT function and make your mark from day one
  • A people-focused culture that values collaboration, expertise and career development
 
Next Steps
If you take your career development seriously, this is the role to do it in. Apply now or call Ty Erasmus at Quinn Allan on 0461 410 477 for a confidential conversation

job.title: Senior Financial Accountant
job.description:
The Opportunity

If you enjoy technical accounting and want a role where your judgement matters, this one is worth a look.

Quinn Allan is partnering with a large, well-established Brisbane organisation to find a Senior Financial Accountant for a 12-month contract starting in November.

This isn’t a role where you’ll spend your days on reconciliations. You’ll be the technical lead across financial accounting, tax, compliance, and treasury. That means working through complex accounting questions, advising on how the standards apply in practice, and making sure the numbers stand up to audit. The organisation’s size and complexity mean there is plenty to get your teeth into. There’s also real scope to leave things better than you found them. The business wants stronger controls, tighter processes and better use of its systems, and you’ll have a hand in shaping how that happens.

What You’ll Be Doing
  • Working through complex accounting issues and advising on how Australian Accounting Standards apply in practice
  • Owning the integrity of the financial statements, general ledger and month-end and year-end close
  • Managing tax obligations and compliance reporting
  • Overseeing treasury, including liquidity, loan facilities, cash reserves and banking relationships
  • Leading the audit process from planning through to closing out findings
  • Reviewing and strengthening accounting policies, procedures and controls
  • Spotting where processes can be redesigned, automated or better supported by systems, and building the business case to make it happen
About You
  • CA or CPA qualified with a relevant tertiary qualification
  • You genuinely enjoy the technical side and are comfortable forming a view on the grey areas
  • Experience leading statutory reporting and audits in a large, complex organisation
  • Solid exposure to tax and treasury
  • An improvement mindset, with a track record of strengthening processes and controls
  • The ability to explain technical matters clearly to people outside finance
  • Experience in a large ERP environment will be highly regarded
If you like solving problems and want your work to make a real difference to how a large organisation manages its finances, this is a rewarding 12 months.

How to Apply

Click apply to submit your resume, or reach out to Matt at Quinn Allan for a confidential conversation about the role.

job.title: Procurement & Supply Chain Manager - Australia

Combining global capability with local expertise, the business partners with many of Australia's leading café, retail and foodservice customers.

Reporting to the Managing Director, Oceania, the Procurement & Supply Chain Manager will be responsible for procurement, purchasing, inventory planning and supply chain activities across the Australian business.

This is a hands-on leadership role that combines strategic oversight with day-to-day execution. You will play an active role in managing supplier relationships, sourcing activities, purchasing, inventory planning and supply continuity while partnering closely with stakeholders across the business.

A key focus of the role will be the management of green coffee spend, the organisation's largest and most strategic procurement category, alongside a broader portfolio of enterprise spend categories.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and implement sourcing and category strategies across key spend areas
  • Lead supplier negotiations and manage supplier relationships locally and internationally
  • Oversee purchasing, inventory planning and inbound supply activities to ensure materials availability and support production requirements
  • Monitor commodity markets, pricing movements, freight trends and supply risks
  • Ensure continuity of supply and strong alignment across procurement, operations, sales and finance
  • Provide commercial input into budgeting, forecasting and business planning activities
  • Partner with global procurement stakeholders to align sourcing strategies and leverage group capability
  • Support ongoing business improvement and transformation initiatives 
About You
You are a commercially minded procurement and supply chain professional who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with operational execution. Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment, you build strong relationships, influence stakeholders and deliver results.

You will bring:
  • Experience leading procurement and supply chain activities within a hands-on operational environment
  • Experience within FMCG, food and beverage manufacturing, agribusiness or another commodity-driven environment
  • Strong supplier management, negotiation and commercial capability
  • Experience managing international suppliers and global supply chains
  • Strong analytical, financial and stakeholder management skills
  • A proactive approach to problem solving and continuous improvement
Experience within the coffee industry or exposure to green coffee procurement will be highly regarded. However, prospective applicants from FMCG, food manufacturing, agribusiness and other commodity-driven environments are encouraged to apply.
 
This is an opportunity to join a highly regarded business at the heart of Australia's coffee industry, where your contribution will be visible, valued and impactful. Local and international travel will be required.

Quinn Allan has been exclusively retained to manage this appointment on behalf of Segafredo Bean Alliance Australia.

job.title: Finance Manager (part-time)
job.description:

Quinn Allan is proud to partner with ACSI (Australian Council of Superannuation Investors), a member-based organisation that provides a strong voice on financially material sustainability and corporate governance risks and opportunities.

Established in 2001, ACSI's members include Australian and international asset owners and institutional investors representing more than $1.9 trillion in funds under management. Through research, company engagement and public policy advocacy, ACSI supports members in exercising active ownership, which enhances the long-term value of the retirement savings entrusted to them to manage, while driving meaningful improvements in corporate sustainability and governance practices of the companies in which they invest.
With a highly engaged, collaborative culture and a clear sense of purpose, ACSI offers the opportunity to contribute to an organisation making a genuine impact across Australia's investment and superannuation landscape.

About the Position
This newly available Finance Manager opportunity has arisen as part of a planned leadership transition within the organisation. Reporting to the Executive Manager, Finance & Corporate Services, the role will take ownership of ACSI's day-to-day finance function while leading a small team and partnering closely with senior stakeholders across the business.
Offered on a 0.6 FTE basis (22.5 hours per week), the position combines technical accounting, financial control, reporting, team leadership and business partnering responsibilities. The successful candidate will play a key role in month-end reporting, budgeting, forecasting, compliance and financial decision-making, while maintaining strong relationships with external advisors and service providers.
Given the size of the organisation, this is a genuinely hands-on role where you'll remain involved in both the preparation and review of financial information while helping develop finance processes, systems and capability across the team.
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced finance professional seeking meaningful work, flexibility and ownership within a respected purpose-led organisation.

Duties
• Lead the day-to-day finance function, including management accounting and financial control
• Prepare and review monthly and quarterly management reporting, analysis and commentary
• Coordinate annual budgeting, forecasting and financial planning processes
• Prepare statutory financial statements and manage the external audit process
• Oversee tax compliance, including BAS, IAS, FBT, payroll tax and related reporting obligations
• Manage payroll governance, reconciliations and relationships with external providers
• Monitor cash flow forecasting and support AFSL financial resource requirements
• Partner with the Executive Management Team on budgeting, reporting and business performance matters
• Manage relationships with auditors, tax advisors, insurers and other external stakeholders
• Lead, mentor and develop two finance team members while building capability across the function
• Support continuous improvement across finance systems, reporting processes and controls
• Assist with governance, compliance and finance-related projects as required

About You
To be successful in this role, you will be a technically strong and hands-on finance professional who enjoys operating in a collaborative, high-accountability environment. You will be comfortable balancing strategic responsibilities with day-to-day financial management while partnering effectively with a broad range of stakeholders.

You will have:
• CA or CPA qualification
• Minimum 5 years' experience in accounting and finance roles
• Strong financial and management accounting capability
• Experience managing month-end reporting, budgeting and forecasting processes

job.title: Senior Accountant
job.description:
About the Company
Quinn Allan is proud to partner with Segafredo Bean Alliance Australia, an established Australian coffee business with a strong presence across the café, hospitality, foodservice and commercial markets.
The business brings together Segafredo Zanetti, a globally recognised Italian coffee brand, with Bean Alliance’s established Australian roasting and distribution operations. Based in Melbourne, the business operates across coffee roasting, sourcing, blending, packaging, wholesale and distribution, supported by a national branch network.
With a diverse portfolio of coffee brands and a broad customer base across Australia, the business operates within a complex, multi-site environment where strong financial management and commercial insight are key to continued performance and growth.

The Opportunity
The business is undergoing an important period of integration and transformation, creating an opportunity for an experienced Senior Accountant to make a genuine impact. Initially, your focus will be firmly on strengthening the finance fundamentals, improving reporting accuracy and implementing appropriate processes and controls to support business growth.
This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys getting into the detail, investigating issues and creating structure in an evolving environment. Once the financial foundations are firmly established, the position will develop into a broader commercial role, providing analysis, insight and decision support across the business.

The Role
Reporting to the CFO and working closely with the Senior Financial Controller, your initial priorities will include:
  • Taking ownership of month-end financial reporting
  • Completing and improving monthly balance sheet reconciliations
  • Strengthening balance sheet integrity and financial controls
  • Preparing accurate and meaningful cash flow forecasts
  • Investigating historical issues, anomalies and accounting discrepancies
  • Improving the accuracy, consistency and timeliness of financial information
  • Supporting budgeting, forecasting and financial planning
  • Monitoring inventory, working capital, margins and cost of goods sold
  • Improving finance processes, systems and reporting disciplines
  • Supporting the continued integration and transformation of the finance function
As reporting accuracy and financial controls improve, the role will increasingly focus on:
  • Financial modelling and commercial analysis
  • Margin, cost and profitability analysis
  • Supporting operational and strategic decision-making
  • Partnering with stakeholders across sales, operations, procurement and supply chain
  • Developing business cases and identifying performance improvement opportunities
About You
You will be a technically capable accountant who understands that strong commercial insight starts with accurate and trusted financial information.
To succeed in this role, you will bring:
  • CA or CPA qualification
  • Strong financial accounting and month-end reporting experience
  • Demonstrated experience managing balance sheet reconciliations and financial controls
  • Strong cash flow forecasting capability
  • The ability to identify issues, investigate anomalies and implement practical solutions
  • Advanced Excel and financial analysis skills
  • Experience with ERP or accounting systems
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
  • A proactive, hands-on and improvement-focused approach
Experience within manufacturing, FMCG, wholesale, distribution or another inventory-based environment will be highly regarded. Exposure to SAP Business One, business integration, systems implementation or finance transformation would also be advantageous.
